subject: MedLytix Dedicated throughput validation & SLO next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ava Shah <ava.shah@medlytix.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated throughput targets and validation plan

Hi Ava — thanks again for the demo today. I wanted to capture the key perf targets you confirmed and propose a short validation plan so we can size the Reserved pool and recommend GPU options. Please confirm any adjustments.

Recap of your targets (as mentioned on call):
- Peak sustained throughput: ~100 requests/sec (RPS) for household inference workload (avg payload ~350 tokens)
- Concurrent active users: 20–30 live connections with streaming enabled
- Latency targets: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms for single-turn responses (~350 tokens). For streaming partial tokens, initial chunk target p50 <= 60ms
- Typical response length: 200–600 tokens (median ~320)
- Batchable workload: small batching preferred to preserve streaming latency; KV-cache reuse anticipated for repeated sessions

Proposed validation plan (48–72 hour window):
1) Sanity run on a 3-node Dedicated pool with A100s (40GB) and H100s (80GB) variants and identical model build
2) Simulated traffic: 100 RPS steady + 30 concurrent streaming sessions with synthetic prompts matching your token distribution
3) Measure: sustained RPS, p50/p95 latency for both non-streaming and streaming initial chunk, GPU utilization, and token cost estimate
4) Deliverable: a short report with recommended reserved throughput (RPS and token/sec), recommended GPU type, and an ops playbook for autoscale/burst policies

Attachments: I included the SLO requirements sheet and a quick call notes PDF. Marcus — can you prepare the GPU eval config (yaml) and a quick test harness we can run in MedLytix staging? Neha — I'll follow up on commercial terms once we have the recommended sizing.

Next steps:
- Ava: confirm the targets above and any blackout windows for testing
- Marcus: provision GPU eval config and test harness
- Stephanie: schedule the 2-day validation window once MedLytix approves

Thanks,
—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated throughput targets and validation plan

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 09:08 AM Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> Marcus — can you prepare the GPU eval config (yaml) and a quick test harness we can run in MedLytix staging?

Yes — attaching the baseline GPU eval config I intend to run. High level notes:
- We'll run two parallel clusters (identical infra except GPU type):
  * 3x NVIDIA A100 40GB nodes
  * 3x NVIDIA H100 80GB nodes
- Model: customer-specified model (we'll use a quantized FP16 path where possible). We'll instrument kernel selection and KV cache hit rates.
- Traffic generator: Phase A (latency-first): 20 concurrent streaming sessions + 20 RPS; Phase B (throughput-first): ramp to 100 RPS steady with 30 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, time-to-first-token (streaming), GPU util, mem temp, tokens/sec, and cost-estimate per 1M tokens.
- Failure modes: simulate node drain and check fallback to compatible model variant (smaller quantized profile)

I'll spin up the harness in our staging cluster and share logs + Grafana dashboard links. Also added a small script to estimate reserved throughput (RPS -> tokens/sec) and recommended headroom (we use 25% buffer for burst protection).

Attachments included: gpu-eval-config.yaml (stub), test-harness-readme.md (inline).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Ava Shah <ava.shah@medlytix.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@medlytix.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated throughput targets and validation plan

Thanks, Stephanie — this looks good and captures what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 100 RPS is a short-term target for the first SaaS region; long-term we'd like to plan for ~200 RPS but can stage to 100 for initial commit
- Latency: p95 target of 300ms is soft; for the highest-value flows (real-time triage) we need p95 <= 200ms if possible. We'd like you to include both scenarios in the report (100 RPS & 200 RPS).
- Streaming: we use early partial responses in the UI; time-to-first-token is critical. Please include measured TTF* (first-token) at p50/p95 in the deliverable.
- Security: we'll place the eval in our VPC staging; Marcus — we'll need the exec-level network instructions and the IAM role ARN for staging access.

We can provide a sample traffic file that matches production prompt mixes; attaching it to this thread. Also, please include cost delta estimates between A100 vs H100 and a smaller quantized L4-class option if you have it.

If everything looks aligned, let's aim to run validation on Oct 19–20 (our staging availability).

Best,
Ava
Ava Shah
Director of Platform Engineering, MedLytix
ava.shah@medlytix.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated throughput targets and validation plan

Perfect — thanks for the quick clarifications, Ava. Summarizing updated scope and owners: 
- Scope: 2-phase validation covering 100 RPS and 200 RPS baselines; measure p50/p95 latency and TTF (streaming), GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens for A100/H100/L4-class.
- Owners: Marcus (test harness & run), Stephanie (scheduling & deliverable), Neha (commercial/commit follow-through), Ava/Ben (staging access + traffic file)
- Dates: Target validation window Oct 19–20 (MedLytix staging). Marcus will need the IAM role ARN and staging endpoint by Oct 16 to provision access.

Action items: 
- Ben: please send staging IAM role ARN and a short list of any egress restrictions by EOD Oct 15
- Marcus: share the Grafana dashboard + a preliminary cost delta table by Oct 16
- Neha: prepare a preliminary reserved throughput proposal (RPS and tokens/sec) and tiered pricing options once Marcus publishes results

I'll create a short one-pager report after the run and share it with your execs. If any of the dates conflict, let me know this week.

Cheers,
—Stephanie
